headline: Claude Code 2.1.232: Six Regression Checks That Matter for Developers
summary: New Claude Code version fixes Windows permission bypasses and enhances context inheritance for forked subagents. Essential checks ensure stability and security.
details: Claude Code 2.1.232 introduces significant changes, including default context and prompt cache inheritance for forked subagents, backgrounding of interactive non-teammate spawns, and patched Windows permission bypasses.

These updates mean that a successful launch is no longer sufficient. Developers must now verify separate operating boundaries, including context inheritance, session routing, permissions, repository trust, MCP probes, and Remote Control recovery.

Key testing procedures involve spawning child agents to confirm correct context inheritance and ensuring interactive spawns move to the background as expected. Session resumption by name also requires verification to prevent messages reaching unintended runs.

Security is enhanced through rigorous permission checks. Testing includes performing a harmless write within an approved path and attempting a denied write to confirm boundary enforcement. Nested repositories also require explicit trust verification, not assuming parent approval.

Further checks cover the reliability of MCP probes and Remote Control recovery, ensuring tools, session state, and recovery messages remain coherent even after failures. A broad end-to-end run might pass while specific regressions in permissions or routing remain hidden.

The article provides a detailed checklist for these regression checks, including official release evidence and rollback boundaries, available at tgwise.com/intelligence/claude-code-2-1-232-forked-subagents-windows-permission-fixes/
